Those handler-vtable-slot identifications are inferred from argument shape (ICATarget target[, LevelCAConfig config]) and call position, and are flagged as such, not claimed at the same confidence as the resolved IFACE/bl calls.

order_confirmed.then: on true, spawns a special-case coroutine referencing a type literally named <MakeFishEatFood>d__16 (confirmed string/type literal in the disassembly) -- i.e. there is at least one handler-specific post-add special case hard-coded into the generic orchestrator.

order_confirmed.likely: LevelCAHandlerBase.OnRemovedFromTarget(ICATarget target) -- called IMMEDIATELY after the list removal succeeds, i.e. BEFORE any target-side cleanup. This is the opposite ordering from Add, where the handler's own hook (OnAddedToTarget) runs LAST, after target-side setup.

cancel_and_complete_cycle.source: the three Spine TrackEntry callbacks registered by CATargetExtensionMethods.PlayContextualAnimation as local functions, plus the shared cleanup local function. Addressable and disassembled individually by their compiler-generated names.

shared_cleanup_EndAnimation_g__0.confirmed: sets ICATarget.CurrentCAPlayType, .CurrentCAConfig and .CurrentCAHandler back (via 3 resolved IFACE setter calls) before a tail call (br x3) onward -- i.e. this is the common 'an animation is no longer the active one' state reset, shared by both the interrupt/cancel and the complete paths below.

cancel_OnInterruptOrEnd_g__1.role: registered as the Spine TrackEntry 'Complete'/interrupt delegate; this is the CANCEL path (fires when a track is interrupted, e.g. a new animation pre-empts the current one, as well as on ordinary non-looped completion of some tracks)
cancel_OnInterruptOrEnd_g__1.confirmed: reads target.ContexualAnimationCounter (IFACE, resolved) and compares it against a counter value captured in the closure when PlayContextualAnimation started; if they differ, this is treated as a STALE callback (a newer animation has since started) and the function returns immediately without touching anything -- a generation-counter guard against races between overlapping animation requests. Only if the counter still matches does it tail-call into EndAnimation.

complete_OnCompleteFullCycle_g__2.role: COMPLETE path for a fully looped animation cycle
complete_OnCompleteFullCycle_g__2.confirmed: fetches the target's current CA handler (via the same interface-cache pattern used elsewhere, IFACE call with selector 0 both times) TWICE in sequence (first attempt, null-ish check, re-fetch) before tail-calling (br x4) a method loaded from the handler's OWN vtable at offset +0x298, with args (handler, target, config).
complete_OnCompleteFullCycle_g__2.likely: LevelCAHandlerBase.OnAnimationFullCycleEnd(ICATarget target, LevelCAConfig config) -- name and signature match exactly; this is also the only base-class method whose name contains 'FullCycle', matching the caller's own compiler-generated name OnCompleteFullCycle.

complete_OnCompleteNotLooped_g__3.role: COMPLETE path for a non-looped (single-shot) animation finishing
confirmed_calls_in_order: ICATarget.get_ContexualAnimationCounter (IFACE) -- same stale-callback guard as the cancel path
conditionally calls OnCompleteFullCycle (bl, resolved) or EndAnimation (bl, resolved) depending on that play type

conditionally calls CATargetExtensionMethods.PlayContextualAnimation again (bl, resolved) -- i.e. this path can re-trigger a new PlayContextualAnimation on completion, which is the mechanism for 'repeat until something else happens' animations (e.g. idle loops composed of non-looped clips)
ends with an unresolved tail call (br x2)
complete_OnCompleteNotLooped_g__3.confidence: high for the resolved calls, open for the final br x2 target

reaction_assets_followup.scope: docs/RECON_CONTEXTUAL_LINKS.md flagged 4 reaction entries across 2 assets needing reconciliation (Bubble_Blower_Tube_L209_Baby_ReactionData's 3 entries and ToddlerBookReadingAnimationsReactionsData2's 1 entry).
reaction_assets_followup.interpretation_added_this_session: Both mismatches are the same shape: the reaction data stores an animation name with the 'CA/' engine prefix already baked in as a literal (e.g. 'CA/General/Look_Around_Amazed'), but the rig's own animation-name inventory (built from the raw Spine skeleton data) lists the name WITHOUT that prefix ('General/Look_Around_Amazed'). This is consistent with 'CA/' being added by LevelCAConfig.CreateAnimationName at runtime on top of whatever the handler's GetFolderName()+name resolves to (confirmed in docs/RECON_CONTEXTUAL_LINKS.md's own 'Construção do nome' section), while these specific ReactionData assets instead store the fully-prefixed string directly as authored data, bypassing CreateAnimationName. If so, the correct rig-membership check for these two entries should strip a leading 'CA/<folder>/' before comparing, which is exactly the alternative the existing audit already found present in the rig. This raises confidence in the existing candidate resolution from 'alternative candidate' to 'best-supported interpretation', but does not change any stored data and was not re-verified by running the verifier with a prefix-stripping rule.
